messages.author: 48f24841e806e6c6
messages.subject: Calling for new developers for rapache
parts:
Hi,

If any of you are interested in helping with rapache, I'd be much
obliged. I've got two tasks that I'd like to accomplish:

1. Package up rapache for the various linux distributions, starting
with debian. I've tried several times in the past to learn how to
create a debian package, and honestly I just get confused and bored
every time. I think the way to aproach this task would be to dissect
one of the many libapache2-mod-* packages.

2. Port rapache to windows and "make it work". This will probably
involve a great deal of work as someone will need to mix and match
compiler tool chains between the apache build and the R build.

Also, if there are any other features you would like to add to
rapache, please let me know. I'm all ears!

Best,

Jeff

messages.author: 832c709713595db0
messages.subject: Re: Calling for new developers for rapache
parts:
Michel Barbosa wrote:
> Hi Jeff,
>
> I just read about Rapache and it seems very promising. I'm about to
> get started with it, any help I can provide? For example, testing etc?

Hy Michel,

Thanks for the offer. If you'd like to tackle testing issues, there are
two areas where your help can be applied:

1. Various make targets like 'make itest', 'make valgrind', and 'make
gdb' work very well interactively, however they could be tightened up a
bit. For instance, after calling 'make itest' a message is produced that
states you should point your browser to a localhost/port combo to start
testing with the links provided in an index.html file. Essentially, I've
crafted a rudimentary set of tests that link off that page to exercise
many important aspects of rapache, but they could be combed through and
enhanced, and new tests can be added if necessary.

2. A more ambitious automated testing framework would be nice such that
a browser is not needed. This may depend on using a command-line browser
such as wget, or even a web client written in R.

Anyways, thanks for your interest and let the list know what kinds of
issues you run into in just getting started. Compiling and installing
rapache can be daunting.

Best,

Jeff
